subject: Re: Order Form — rapid subpoena & indemnity playbook
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novahealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Dwyer <mark.dwyer@novahealth.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Initial order form questions — potential third-party subpoena scenario

Olga,

Thanks for the updated order form. Two quick asks from our side as we prep procurement:

1) We need clarity on how Redwood would respond if we receive a third-party subpoena alleging that generated outputs infringe a patent. Specifically: who handles litigation coordination vs. the customer?

2) Can Redwood confirm a contact and SLA for evidence preservation and an initial 48–72 hour response window? Our legal team will need this in the procurement packet.

Mark and procurement are copied. Attaching a short checklist of what our legal team expects. Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement | NovaHealth

Attachment: nova_procurement_checklist.pdf (referenced)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial order form questions — potential third-party subpoena scenario

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers below, and I'll route fuller legal language once we sync with counsel.

- Responsibility: Redwood proposes to defend and control the defense for third-party IP claims that arise from our model outputs where the claim is based on Redwood-hosted model behavior. That said, for claims tied to customer-supplied prompts or customer-uploaded data, we expect cooperation and potential handback.

- Evidence + SLA: We can commit to acknowledging an evidence preservation request within 24 hours and an initial packet within 72 hours for most requests. If litigation counsel is engaged, we may need a bit more time to pull privileged materials and coordinate with our infra teams.

I've looped in Kim and Ben to prepare redlines to the Order Form and a short playbook for subpoenas/evidence collection. Expect redline PDF and draft playbook by EOD tomorrow.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Draft redlines + subpoena playbook (internal)

Team — attaching draft OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf and a working document for a subpoena-response-playbook.docx. Key negotiation positions called out here:

- Narrow the "defend" trigger to exclude outputs generated from Customer-provided proprietary training data or content where Customer had sole control of the prompt pipeline. (This avoids blanket defense obligations.)
- Preserve Redwood's right to lead the defense (defend/control) but add an explicit cooperation requirement and a short notice window from the customer (7 business days) to permit technical triage.
- Add a slot for escrow or insurance offset language for third-party damages over a threshold.
- Evidence handling: commit to 24-hour ack / 72-hour initial packet, with a clause that additional privileged logs may require counsel coordination and a DPA amendment if cross-border data is implicated.

Questions for Neha/legal counsel: are we comfortable with a 7 business day notice obligation from customers? Also proposing a separate exhibit that outlines required evidence types and a template notice.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf; subpoena-response-playbook.docx; evidence-request-template.docx

From: Mark Dwyer <mark.dwyer@novahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@novahealth.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft redlines + subpoena playbook (internal)

Kim — thanks for this — NovaHealth legal has one concern: 7 business days is long for notice when there's a live subpoena. Our counsel asks for a 48 hour preliminary notice if a customer becomes aware of an active subpoena so they can start preservation and meet court deadlines.

Also, how would Redwood handle costs for a preservation effort that requires custom engineer time (e.g., creating a one-off snapshot of logs)? Would that be billable or covered under the defense? Our procurement team needs clarity for budgeting.

If you can add a short appendix that lists response SLAs and estimated engineering effort buckets (tier 1: log retrieval under 2 hours; tier 2: 2–8 hours; tier 3: >8 hours), that would be very helpful.

–Mark
Head of Legal Ops (NovaHealth)

Attachment: none

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mark Dwyer <mark.dwyer@novahealth.com>, Elena Soto <elena.soto@novahealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft redlines + subpoena playbook (internal)

Mark / Elena — appreciate the prompt feedback. Quick responses to the two asks:

1) Notice window: we can accept a dual-tier notice approach in the Order Form: a 48-hour "initial notice" for active subpoenas (basic metadata + subpoena copy) and a 7-business-day window for full cooperation materials to allow Redwood to triage and prepare privileged materials. We'll add suggested language.

2) Engineering effort / cost: Redwood will provide a baseline preservation response (ack + standard packet) at no cost. For bespoke engineering tasks (tier 2/3) we propose either time-and-materials billing or a capped pass-through fee; alternatively, customer can pre-purchase an "e-discovery" support bundle in the Order Form. We'll add a short table of typical effort buckets and a sample price carve-out in the appendix.

Next steps (proposed):
- Kim to update the redline with the dual-tier notice + evidence appendix.
- Olga / Neha to sign off on defense/control language and insurance/escrow threshold.
- I'll prepare a short one-page elevator summary of the playbook for procurement to include in the packet.

If you want to fast-track, I can join a 30-minute call tomorrow at 9am PT to walk through.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments: subpoena-response-playbook.docx (updated)
